name: Training the Beast
summary: Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young tauren hunters in Mulgore. After demonstrating the spiritual patience and resolve required to soothe the wild beasts of the plains, hunters are sent to Thunder Bluff to learn the lifelong discipline of bonding with, nourishing, and commanding a permanent animal companion.

sections.title: The Path to the Great Bluff
sections.body: Having successfully tested their spirit against the dangerous predators of Mulgore—plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops—tauren hunters are judged ready for the true mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, the mentor in Bloodhoof Village, entrusts the novice with a journey to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There stands Holt Thunderhorn, a legendary figure among the shu'halo whose reputation for communing with the wilds is surpassed only by his reverence for the Earthmother.

sections.title: A Sacred Bond
sections.body: To the tauren, a beast is not a simple weapon or thrall; it is a partner granted through harmony with the natural world. Holt Thunderhorn imparts the vital knowledge required to sustain this partnership. A hunter must learn not only how to guide the creature's combat instincts, but how to nourish its body through regular feeding, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back should it fall defending its companion on the plains.

faq.q: Who do I speak to for this quest?
faq.answer: You must speak with Holt Thunderhorn, a master hunter located atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. Yaw Sharpmane directs you to him once your initial trials of taming wild beasts in Mulgore are complete.

faq.q: What skills do tauren hunters learn upon completing this quest?
faq.answer: Holt Thunderhorn teaches you how to train your pet in new abilities, how to feed your companion to keep it loyal and content, and how to revive your pet should it perish in combat.

faq.q: Where does this quest fit in the tauren hunter chain?
faq.answer: This is the final quest in the sequence. It follows The Hunter's Path and the three-part trial of Taming the Beast, where the hunter temporarily pacifies an adult plainstrider, a prairie stalker, and a swoop across the plains.

faq.q: Why does Holt Thunderhorn hold such high standing among tauren hunters?
faq.answer: Holt has spent a lifetime testing himself against Azeroth's most ferocious beasts, commanding multiple powerful companions while maintaining a deep spiritual bond with the Earthmother. His wisdom makes him the principal teacher for young shu'halo hunters in Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Can hunters tame their permanent pet before turning in this quest?
aliases: can i tame a pet now
when do i get my pet
do i need training the beast
faq.answer: You already have the power to tame wild beasts from the previous trial, but until you speak to Holt Thunderhorn, you lack the knowledge to feed, revive, or teach skills to your chosen companion.

faq.q: Why is pet care tied to the Earthmother in tauren culture?
faq.answer: Tauren see all living creatures as children of the Earthmother. A hunter does not dominate a beast through sheer force of will, but enters into a spiritual covenant where the hunter provides food and care in exchange for the animal's loyalty and protection.

angles.text: This rite marks the transition from fighting alone to fighting beside a loyal companion, completing your fundamental training as a warden of the wilderness.
For the shu'halo, taking an animal companion into battle carries a sacred duty of stewardship and respect for the creations of the Earthmother.
